title: Mizzen trust report
description: `trust.json` in the output folder: a build identifier plus one entry per rendered content page, keyed by the page URL including `base`. Keys are sorted by code point. Every entry names its stable `key`, its `url`, its `source`, the state of each evidence signal, `level`, `reasons`, and, when known, `lastReviewer`, in that order. `build.id` is a deterministic hash of the rendered pages, so evidence can be joined to the build that produced them. Two builds with the same model, data, root, and `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` write the same bytes. App and asset pages are left out.

build.description: The identity of the rendered pages the evidence belongs to.

id.description: SHA-256 over every doc page's key, Markdown hash, and HTML hash, sorted by URL. Changing a page's URL, source, Markdown, or HTML changes it.

pages.description: How many rendered content pages the build has.
One entry per rendered content page, keyed by the page URL including `base`, in code-point order.

key.description: Stable page key: SHA-256 of the page's URL, a NUL, and its source file. The same page has the same key across builds.

source.description: The source file, relative to the site root, with forward slashes.

evidence.description: What each signal measured, or why it did not. `missing` means no source for the signal existed; `unknown` means a source existed but gave no answer. A signal that is not `measured` also has an explaining reason.

examples.description: `measured`, `none` when the page declares no test fence, or `unknown` when it declares examples but their result is unavailable.

drift.description: `measured`, `missing` when no drift data or root was available, or `unknown` when a check was available but gave no answer.

review.description: `measured`, `missing` when no reviewer data or root was available, or `unknown` when the source named no readable date.

level.description: The worst level the reasons support: `at-risk` beats `review-due` beats `verified`.

reasons.description: Exactly three reasons, in the fixed order examples, drift, review.

lastReviewer.description: The author name of the last commit that touched the page's source, when git or the data file names one; absent otherwise.

code.description: A stable identifier for one finding. `examples.unknown` is the output's own code: the page declares examples but their result is unavailable, so the page cannot be verified.

message.description: The sentence a maintainer reads to see what the code found.
